passage: Hemant let go of his father's hand for one second to look at a kite, and when he looked up the bazaar was all strangers' legs. His heart thudded. He closed his eyes. "Where was I holding his hand? The sweet shop with the jalebi pans. And the blue gate next to it." He reasoned that Papa would look back along the way they had come, and the sweet shop was the one place they both knew. So he walked, not ran, past two stalls, stopped by the blue gate and stood still. Sunaina Aunty from the sweet shop noticed and handed him a stool. Soon his father's checked shirt came through the crowd.

qa.q: Which two landmarks did Hemant remember?
qa.a: He remembered the sweet shop and the blue gate.

qa.q: What was Hemant thinking as he closed his eyes to recall the way?
qa.a: He was calming himself and working out where he had last held his father's hand.

qa.q: What else could Hemant do if his father does not come soon, and why?
qa.a: He could ask Sunaina Aunty to phone his father, because a shop owner at a fixed spot is an easy, safe helper.

qa.q: How might Hemant's father look for him?
qa.a: His father would probably retrace their steps too, going to where they were last together, so the landmark gives them a good chance to meet.

grounding: A boy recalls the landmarks near where he last held his father's hand and calmly returns to them.

passage:
"Gautam bhaiya, where's Chachu?"
"Don't cry, Imran. Stand here with me. Hold my hand."
"Everyone's so tall. I can't see."
"Wait. Think. When did we last have Chachu's hand?"
"When we got jalebi?"
"Yes. The sweet shop. And next to it..."
"The blue gate! With the lion on top!"
"Right. So if Chachu is looking, where will he go?"
"Back to the sweet shop?"
"That's where we'll go. Slowly. No running."
They walked, hand in hand, keeping the shops on their left.
"Bhaiya! The lion!"
By the blue gate, Chachu was turning in circles, calling their names.

qa.q: What was on top of the blue gate?
How was Imran feeling when he couldn't see Chachu?
qa.a: Imran was frightened and close to tears, overwhelmed by the tall crowd.

qa.q: What else could Gautam do if Chachu was not at the blue gate?
qa.a: He could ask the sweet shop owner to call Chachu, and wait there with Imran.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Chachu?
qa.a: Chachu is frightened, turning in circles and calling, and must feel huge relief when the boys appear.

grounding: It shows a boy recalling the sweet shop and blue gate where they last held his uncle's hand and calmly heading back to that landmark.

passage: Last Diwali, at the big market in Karol Bagh, I let go of Papa's hand to look at a toy car, and when I turned back he was gone. My sister Dilnaz was with him, not me. I felt my knees go weak. Then I made myself think. "Where was I holding his hand? At the sweet shop with the huge kaju katli stack. And there was a blue gate beside it." I could still see the gate over the heads, three shops back. "If Papa is looking, he'll go back to where we were." So I walked there, slowly, not running. Papa was already at the blue gate, with Dilnaz on his shoulders, shouting, "Darshan!" I have never been so happy to see a gate.

qa.q: Where did Darshan let go of Papa's hand?
qa.a: To look at a toy car, near the sweet shop.

qa.q: How did Darshan feel when Papa was gone?
qa.a: Darshan felt weak-kneed and frightened, then calmer after deciding what to do.

qa.q: What else could Darshan do if the gate had been out of sight?
qa.a: Darshan could stop and ask the sweet shop owner to call Papa, rather than walk around looking.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Dilnaz on Papa's shoulders?
qa.a: Dilnaz can see over the crowd and is probably scared too, and then relieved when the missing sibling appears.

grounding: It shows a child recalling the sweet shop and blue gate where the family last held hands and heading calmly back to that landmark.
